title: How Vacation Rental Property Managers Automate Financial Operations with Ramp + Topkey
summary: Best Ramp integration for short-term rental property managers. Topkey automates receipt capture, eliminates manual data entry, and streamlines month-end close.
body_markdown:
If you're a short-term rental property manager, you know the pain. Your team uses Ramp cards to earn rewards and manage expenses across properties. But transactions pile up throughout the month with zero context. There's no property attribution, no category, no indication of whether they're owner charges or corporate expenses. As you grow, a hundred transactions turn into thousands. Your team now spends 5-7 days, sometimes 2 weeks, hunting down what each charge was for, categorizing manually, and entering data twice across your PMS and accounting software.


The problem isn't Ramp. It's the gap between Ramp and the systems short-term rental property managers rely on. The[Ramp + Topkey integration](https://topkey.io/features/bring-your-own-card) closes this gap by capturing transaction context at purchase and syncing it automatically to both systems. In this article, we'll walk through how a disconnected, manual expense process breaks month-end close and how the integration reclaims the days your team spends on manual reconciliation.


## The Manual Work Slowing Month-End Close


Here's the problem Ramp and Topkey solve together. Your team uses Ramp cards throughout the month. Charges accumulate in Ramp. Without an integration, that data isn't flowing into your PMS or accounting software. But even worse: each charge sits with zero context. A $50 charge at Home Depot. A $120 at Lowe's. Your finance team has no idea which property each belongs to, whether it should be billed to owners, or what category it should be coded to. By month-end, you have thousands of contextless transactions waiting.


Each one needs to be matched to the right property, coded correctly, manually entered into your PMS, and then manually entered again into your accounting software. And it has to be done without error. Thousands of charges. Two separate manual entries for each one. You're pinging your team asking them questions about purchases they made three weeks ago and which unit each one was for. You buckle up knowing month-end close is about to consume at least a full week of your team's time just to hope that you got everything right.


For an operator managing 120+ properties, five to seven extra days of month-end work is the cost. The Ramp + Topkey integration eliminates it entirely. Here's the workflow top STR operators run.


## The Ramp + Topkey Workflow


Instead of your team dealing with contextless charges and spending month-end hunting down which property each receipt belongs to, here's what actually happens when Ramp and Topkey connect.


### Create Virtual Ramp Cards inside Topkey


You don't have to log into Ramp to issue cards.[Create virtual Ramp cards directly from Topkey](https://topkey.io/features/bring-your-own-card) , set spending limits, assign cardholders, and the card is issued in Ramp. Your entire team deploys cards from one place with no context-switching.


### Context Captured at Point of Sale, not After


When a charge happens, Topkey reads the transaction data from Ramp instantly, capturing vendor, amount, date, and cardholder information. The employee who made the charge gets a text with a link to Topkey.


They click through to Topkey,[upload the receipt](https://topkey.io/features/pms-automations) , tag the property, select the category, and mark it as owner-billable or corporate. All of this happens at that moment. The receipt and complete transaction context are captured before the cardholder even leaves the store.


By the time month-end arrives, everything is already there in Topkey. Already coded. Already attributed to the right property. Just awaiting review and approval. Your finance team gets transactions with complete context, not contextless charges sitting in Ramp that need to be hunted down. They're reviewing and approving what's been captured and coded in Topkey instead of spending hours tracking down which property each charge belongs to, recoding transactions, or guessing at what should go where.


### Approval Workflow Automates the Gate


Before any Ramp card charge touches QBO or your PMS, it sits in[Topkey's approval workflow](https://topkey.io/features/approval-workflows) . Transactions that meet your approval exemptions flow downstream with no review needed. Anything outside those parameters, such as an amount outside your normal range, a new vendor, or a high-dollar transaction, routes to your team for review. Once all required approvals are complete, the data is ready to sync.


### Data Synced to Your PMS and Accounting Software


Once approved, Topkey syncs the transaction to your PMS automatically. For accounting software, you trigger the sync to QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, or your accounting platform when you're ready. No manual re-entry. No re-coding. Everything that was captured and coded at point of sale flows downstream exactly as intended.


### Month-End Turns into a Breeze


At month-end, all Ramp transactions are already in Topkey with complete context. Every charge is tagged to the correct property. Every transaction is properly categorized. Receipts are attached. Owner-billable expenses are flagged. And approvals are complete. Your finance team reviews clean, fully-contextualized data that's organized exactly how they need it, ready to flow directly to your accounting software. What used to be a week-long property-hunting, re-entry marathon, and spreadsheet scramble now takes hours.


### Proven Workflow Your Team Can Repeat Monthly


Your finance team has a repeatable[financial operating system](https://topkey.io/expense-management) built specifically for short-term rental operators. One they can trust as they continue to grow. Month after month, the same process delivers a predictable, manageable month-end close. That's why top enterprise vacation rental operators leverage Ramp and Topkey together.


## Results Using Ramp + Topkey Integration


Property tags, expense categories, and owner-billable flags are captured at the moment of purchase, not chased down weeks later. Automatic syncs eliminate manual re-entry into your PMS and accounting. The results are immediate. Here's what operators see.


### Month-End Close without the Chaos


When month-end arrives, everything is ready to review in Topkey. All Ramp transactions are there with proper property tags, expense categorization, attached receipts, and owner-billable charges flagged. Your finance team reviews and approves clean data. No hunting for context, no recoding, no manual re-entry. Once approved, transactions flow automatically to your accounting software and PMS, and owner statements are generated with accurate expense data. Reconciliation shifts from a data-entry scramble to straightforward review and approval, reclaiming significant time every month.


### Scalability without Breakdown


Manual expense work doesn't scale linearly. It compounds. An operator managing 50 properties spends days on month-end. At 150 properties, that process stretches to weeks. As you add properties, manual tagging, categorization, and re-entry tasks multiply. Without a bridge between systems, growth means more reconciliation work, not less. With Topkey, context is captured at point of sale the same way for every property. Your finance team's process stays consistent regardless of how many properties you manage.


### Accuracy and Owner Billing


When property tags and owner-billable flags are captured at the moment of purchase, your owner statements are built on accurate data. Owner charges are correctly identified and billed. Your accounting records match reality. Every charge has a documented trail showing when it happened, which property it belongs to, how it's categorized, and who approved it. Operators report that accurate owner-billable tracking increases the amount they can bill to owners by up to 15-25%, as charges stop slipping through without proper attribution. More accurate billing means more revenue recovered every month.


### One Centralized Hub to Manage Finances


[Topkey](https://topkey.io/) becomes the hub where your financial operations live. Ramp card expenses flow in automatically, tagged and categorized at point of sale. But[expense management](https://topkey.io/expense-management) is just the start. Beyond expense management, Topkey supports[bill pay](https://topkey.io/bill-pay) ,[inventory management](https://topkey.io/inventory-management) , and[revenue reconciliation](https://topkey.io/revenue-reconciliation) , all built specifically for STR operations. As you grow, operators often find themselves adding these tools to Topkey and building out their entire financial system in one place. As Julio Clavijo, CFO at[Otium](https://stayotium.com/) , explains, "We connected our Ramp cards to Topkey, because Topkey is the main hub where our financial operations happen." Everything flows through one system, so every dollar is tracked, every approval is clear, and your finance team has complete visibility into the business.


### Keep Your Ramp Rewards


Ramp and Topkey were built to work together. Ramp does what it does best, issues cards and earns you rewards. Topkey does what it does best for STR operators. It adds the context layer every charge needs by capturing property tags, expense categories, and owner-billable flags at point of sale, then syncing everything to your PMS and accounting software automatically. Your team spends. Topkey captures it, codes it, and routes it to the right owner or property without manual work. Everything happens in one place, and the rewards pile up.


## How to Setup Ramp + Topkey Integration


Here's how to get the integration running. As a Topkey customer, you'll connect your Ramp account to Topkey, sync your cards and properties, and start creating virtual cards. All without leaving Topkey. The whole process takes about five minutes. Let's walk through it.


### How to Connect Ramp & Topkey


- Open your Topkey profile dropdown in the top left and click "Settings."
- Navigate to "Integrations" on the Settings page.
- Find "Ramp" under "Other integrations" and click it.
- You'll be redirected to Ramp's login page; log in with your Ramp account.
- Click "Authorize" on Ramp's site to approve the connection.
- You'll be brought back to Topkey.
- If you have multiple Ramp entities, select "All Entities" or a specific entity to scope the connection. Single-entity accounts skip this automatically.
- Once complete, you can create virtual Ramp cards directly from Topkey.


That's it. Your Ramp account is now connected to Topkey. Next, you'll sync your cards and properties so Topkey has everything it needs to manage your expenses.


### Sync Ramp Cards into Topkey


Once Ramp is connected, a single sync pull imports your latest cards, cardholders, and your PMS properties. From that moment on, Topkey knows which card belongs to which person and which properties exist to tag. Everything syncs automatically on a schedule you set, so you never have to re-enter the same data twice.


### Running Your First Ramp Sync


The first sync is where everything connects. It pulls all your Ramp data into Topkey and links it to your properties. Here's the step-by-step process:


- Open the Cards section from Topkey's main navigation.
- Click "Sync Ramp Cards" in the top action bar.
- Topkey imports all your Ramp cards and cardholders.
- Topkey sends a welcome email to any new cardholders and archives inactive cards.
- Run the sync again anytime to refresh Topkey with the latest data from Ramp.


From now on, you can set this sync to run automatically on a schedule, so your cards and properties stay current. Here's exactly what gets synced every time you run it.


### What Gets Synced and When


Each sync pulls the card details, cardholders, roles, and vendor information Topkey needs to manage your expenses. Topkey enforces the same spending limits and permissions as Ramp, and vendors sync so you can manage bill pay without recreating lists. The sync runs on a schedule you set, keeping everything current without manual re-entry. Next, learn how to create virtual cards for new team members directly inside Topkey.


### Create Virtual Ramp Cards from inside Topkey


Bringing on a new maintenance contractor? Onboarding a property manager? You never have to log into Ramp.[Create the card directly in Topkey](https://topkey.io/features/bring-your-own-card) , set the spending limit, assign the cardholder, and the card is issued in Ramp instantly. Your entire team deploys cards from one place, no bouncing between Ramp and Topkey.


Here's a step-by-step guide on how to issue a virtual Ramp card in Topkey:


- Open the Cards section from Topkey's navigation.
- Click "Create Ramp Card" in the top action bar.
- Select the cardholder from the dropdown (they must already be synced from Ramp).
- Create a display name for the card, for example "Maintenance for Property 42."
- Set the spending limit you want to enforce.
- Choose your auto-sync interval so Topkey refreshes this card's data from Ramp on your schedule.
- Click "Create Card."
- The card appears in your Topkey cards list and is issued in Ramp.


Key prerequisite: The cardholder must be synced to Topkey from Ramp first. If they don't appear in the dropdown, make sure they're in Ramp, then click "Sync Ramp Cards" to bring them into Topkey before creating the card.


Now that you can create virtual Ramp cards in Topkey, learn how to manage them.


### Manage Card Lifecycle without Leaving Topkey


Every Ramp card appears in Topkey with its current status. Suspend, unsuspend, or terminate cards instantly without logging into Ramp. When a property manager leaves, a contractor ends, or a card is lost, you control access immediately. If they return, unsuspend the card. Everything stays in Topkey, so your financial hub stays secure and current without system-switching.


## Who this Integration is Built For


At every scale of STR operation, the month-end story is the same. Your team uses Ramp cards to earn rewards, but transactions arrive with zero context. There's no property attribution, no category, no indication of whether they're owner charges. Getting that data into your PMS and accounting requires manual entries and hours adding the missing context. As you scale, this problem compounds. More properties mean more contextless transactions, more manual work, more dual-entry mistakes, and more cash leakage.


The integration captures context at point of sale and eliminates dual-entry. Transactions flow to both systems as a single entry. By month-end, everything is already coded and ready. The work doesn't multiply with scale because most of it happens upfront and is automated. Your finance team runs the same repeatable process every month. Add 100 properties, and month-end feels the same. The work stays predictable, not the chaos. That's the difference between scaling feeling overwhelming and feeling routine.


## Close the Gap with Topkey + Ramp


The gap between Ramp and your PMS and accounting software is where month-end chaos lives. Close it and everything changes. Context is captured at point of sale by your team, manual dual-entry is eliminated, and data flows automatically to both systems. Your finance team stops hunting for property tags and categorization. For an operator managing 120 properties, that's six days of work reclaimed every month.

## FAQ


### 1. Do I have to migrate off my PMS, accounting software, or Ramp?


No. Your PMS, accounting software, and Ramp all stay exactly where they are. Topkey layers in between them as a connector. Your existing tools keep running. Ramp card data flows into Topkey, gets coded and approved, then syncs downstream to your PMS and accounting software automatically. You keep the systems you know and trust. Topkey bridges the gaps between them to help you close out month-end without the chaos.


### 2. Which accounting software does Topkey work with?


Topkey syncs with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Xero, Sage Intacct, and NetSuite. When you're ready to close your books, Ramp transactions flow to your accounting software with full property coding and expense categorization already assigned. Your finance team receives clean, organized data ready to post. Everything that was captured and categorized at point of sale in Topkey arrives in your accounting software exactly as intended.


### 3. How long does setup take?


Setup takes about five minutes to connect Ramp and Topkey via OAuth. A single sync pull imports your Ramp cards, cardholders, properties from your PMS, and Ramp vendors into Topkey. From that moment on, every Ramp card charge lands in Topkey with full context and real-time visibility. No manual configuration needed beyond that initial connection.


### 4. Do I have to manually import my ramp card data into my PMS?


Not with the Topkey and Ramp connected. Many property managers currently using Ramp have to export card transactions as spreadsheets and manually import them into their PMS, property by property. Topkey eliminates this entirely. Ramp card transactions are pulled automatically, matched to the correct property through your PMS integration, and synced directly into your workflow. No spreadsheets or manual imports. No more lost time during the month-end.


### 5. Can I create virtual Ramp cards in Topkey?


Create virtual Ramp cards directly in Topkey without logging into Ramp. Set spending limits, assign cardholders, name the card, and it's provisioned instantly. Virtual card spend is tracked, categorized, and approved through the same workflow as physical cards, with full property attribution and receipt capture at point of sale.


### 6. Does Ramp integrate with Track?


No. Ramp has no native Track (TravelNet Solutions) integration, so managers running both export card transactions to CSV and import them into Track by hand, property by property. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the property, coded, and approved, then sync into Track with attribution applied. Because Track drives owner statements, miscoded property spend becomes an owner problem, not just a reconciliation one. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.


### 7. Does Ramp integrate with Guesty?


No. Ramp has no native Guesty integration, so card spend sits outside the PMS entirely and gets reconciled later with no listing-level attribution. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the Guesty listing, coded, and approved, then sync with attribution applied. Because Guesty is built for reservations and listings rather than accounts payable, expenses never carry property detail on their own. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.


### 8. Does Ramp integrate with Streamline?


No. Ramp has no native Streamline VRS integration, so managers running both rekey card transactions into Streamline by hand or build spreadsheets to bulk import them. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the property, coded, and approved, then sync into Streamline with attribution applied. Because Streamline already runs accounting and expenses in-house, everything downstream depends on that data landing accurately. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.


### 9. Does Ramp integrate with Hostaway?


No. Ramp has no native Hostaway integration, so managers running both export card transactions and match them to properties by hand after the fact. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the property, coded, and approved, then sync into Hostaway with attribution applied. Because Hostaway is built for channel distribution and day-to-day operations rather than expense accounting, manual coding is usually the first thing to break as a portfolio grows. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.


### 10. Does Ramp integrate with Hospitable?


No. Ramp has no native Hospitable integration, so card spend gets tracked in spreadsheets and reconciled well after the charge happened. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the property, coded, and approved, then sync into Hospitable with attribution applied. Managers running Hospitable have usually automated guest messaging, pricing, and turnovers already — expenses are the last thing still done by hand. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.


### 11. Does Ramp integrate with OwnerRez?


No. Ramp has no native OwnerRez integration, so card transactions get exported and attributed to properties manually before owner statements go out. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the property, coded, and approved, then sync into OwnerRez with attribution applied. Because OwnerRez feeds owner-facing reporting, a charge coded to the wrong property surfaces in front of an owner rather than staying an internal cleanup. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.


### 12. Does Ramp integrate with Hostfully?


No. Ramp has no native Hostfully integration, so card spend lives outside the PMS and gets reassembled at month-end from statements and receipts. Topkey connects the two. Ramp charges land in Topkey as they post, get matched to the property, coded, and approved, then sync into Hostfully with attribution applied. Because Hostfully covers operations and the guest experience rather than accounts payable, expense detail otherwise never reaches the property record. Topkey catches it at point of sale, receipt attached.
